title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Determination of the filtered Dieudonné module of the Lubin–Tate group.' Setting: K/Q_p is finite with ring of integers A, residue field k = F_q (q = p^f), uniformiser π and [K:Q_p] = h = ef. W = W(k) is the maximal unramified subring, giving Z_p ⊂ W ⊂ A with degrees f and e.

The overall goal is to compute the filtered Dieudonné module (Dieudonné crystal plus Hodge filtration) of the Lubin–Tate formal A-module. This is presumably a test case for the 'mysterious functor' programme of 1970, which seeks to relate p-divisible groups over A to Galois representations and filtered Dieudonné modules.

Step 1 (special fibre, the only step carried out on this page). Classify Barsotti–Tate groups G_0 over k of height h with an A-action such that π acts as F^f, the q-Frobenius of G_0 relative to F_q. By contravariant Dieudonné theory these correspond to:
- free W-modules M of rank h;
- a σ-linear F_M;
- an A-action λ ↦ λ_M by W-endomorphisms commuting with F_M;
- (*) F_M^f = π_M;
- (*') there exists V_M with F_M V_M = V_M F_M = p.
The two module structures combine into a module structure over A_W = A ⊗_{Z_p} W. With σ_A = id ⊗ σ, F_M is the same as a σ_A-linear endomorphism satisfying (*) and (*'). The page stops here.

The natural continuation, which is not on this page, runs as follows.
- Since W ⊂ A, A_W ≅ ∏_{i∈Z/f} A, with σ_A permuting the factors cyclically. So M = ⊕ M_i, and F maps M_i to M_{i+1}.
- W-rank counting (A has W-rank e) shows each M_i is free of rank 1 over A. F is then given by elements a_i ∈ A with ∏ a_i = π.
- Condition (*') holds automatically, since p ∈ πA. Exactly one a_i is a uniformiser and the others are units, which can be normalised away.
- So G_0 is unique up to isomorphism, of dimension dim M/FM = 1. This is the reduction of the Lubin–Tate group.
- The filtered module is then obtained from a lift to A via deformation theory, giving the known D_cris of the Lubin–Tate character.
errors: No error on the page itself. Implicitly, F_M^f is W-linear because σ^f = id on W(F_q), so (*) makes sense; this is left tacit.

Gap for the intended continuation: evaluating the Dieudonné crystal on A, to obtain the Hodge filtration on M ⊗_W A, needs a divided-power argument (Grothendieck–Messing). A direct nilpotent PD thickening A → k is unavailable when e > p−1. This is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Classification of p-divisible groups over F_q with formal A-module structure such that π = F^f, via Dieudonné modules over A ⊗_{Z_p} W with σ_A-semilinear Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné module of a formal O_K-module / Lubin–Tate special fibre; splitting O_K ⊗_{Z_p} W ≅ ∏ O_K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lubin–Tate (1965); Dieudonné-module treatment by Hazewinkel, Drinfeld (1974–76), Fontaine (1977)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related remarks in 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970, publ. 1974); not this computation as far as known

missed.claim: Historical evidence that around 1970 Grothendieck began explicitly testing the 'mysterious functor' idea on the Lubin–Tate group, by computing its filtered Dieudonné module. This predates Fontaine's systematic treatment. The computation itself is standard today.
missed.quote: Détermination du module de Dieudonné filtré du groupe de Lubin-Tate.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the origin of filtered-Dieudonné-module thinking in Grothendieck's crystal notes, relevant to the history of p-adic Hodge theory; no new mathematics.

missed.claim: The page sets up the special-fibre classification but breaks off before the uniqueness argument and before the Hodge filtration, i.e. the lift to A.
missed.quote: Alors la donnée de F_M équivaut à la donnée d'un endom. σ_A-linéaire, satisfaisant (*) (*')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Not mathematically: the completion is textbook material now.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine Dieudonné-theoretic setup that has since become standard. The interest is purely historical: Grothendieck targeted the filtered Dieudonné module of Lubin–Tate around 1970, anticipating Fontaine's programme.
transcription_corrections: 'hauteur (= v. ρ)' is probably a parenthetical such as '(= rang de M)'; it is illegible and should be marked uncertain.
'automorphisme de Frobenius' is more likely 'endomorphisme de Frobenius de G_0/F_q', since Frobenius on G_0 is an isogeny, not an automorphism.
In 'endom σ-linéaire' the margin addition 'M' belongs to 'modules libres M de rang h sur W'; the object is 'avec endom. σ-linéaire (σ autom. de Frob. de W) F_M'.
'π_{G_0} = F^f': the leftover struck characters before F_M^f in (*) are deletions and can be ignored.
